subject: Urgent: Logitica embeddings latency spike after catalog rollout
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@logitica.com>
To: mina.haddad@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: 2027-11-03T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Sudden latency spike — embeddings p95/p99 after yesterday's catalog update

Hi Mina / Jonas,

We've been seeing a major regression on the embeddings endpoint since the catalog rollout you did yesterday (model_catalog v20271102-4). Starting ~03:30 UTC this morning our p95 and p99 jumped sharply and error rate climbed. Quick numbers from our side (US-WEST requests):
- Baseline (prior 7 days): p95 ~ 350ms, p99 ~ 900ms, errors ~0.3%
- Today (since 03:30 UTC): p95 ~ 1.8s, p99 ~ 5.2s, errors ~4.6%

Attached is a screenshot from our monitoring and a small trace file with sample trace/span ids for recent failed calls (trace-span-ids.txt). Sample request ids: req_8a3f1e2, req_8a3f1e7, req_8a3f3c1. We rely on embeddings heavily for search ranking and this is impacting production traffic — several customers are complaining.

Can you confirm whether the new quantized variant or kernel selection in the catalog could have affected serving behavior? We need an urgent mitigation (rollback or routing to the previous artifact) and a postmortem. Please escalate to execs if needed.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Engineering — Logitica

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: sean.gallagher@redwood.com
Date: 2027-11-03T09:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency spike — embeddings p95/p99 after yesterday's catalog update

Thanks Elena — sorry you're seeing this. Jonas and I are on it and we've looped infra and SRE. Preliminary ask: can you confirm whether affected traffic is only US-WEST or also EU?

What we're going to do immediately:
- Triage the rollout candidate (v20271102-4) to see kernel/quantization changes.
- If we see a clear correlation, we'll roll traffic back to the previous catalog artifact (v20271101-9) and can route Logitica traffic to that variant within ~30 minutes.
- We'll also open an incident ticket and share a timeline and postmortem.

Jonas — please own the customer comms thread (I'll send an external update once we confirm the plan). Marcus / Neha / Rishi — can you triage stack traces and infra metrics (queues, batch times, KV cache misses) and confirm whether this is a model runtime regression or an orchestration/batching issue?

Mina
Sr. Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: mina.haddad@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2027-11-03T09:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency spike — embeddings p95/p99 after yesterday's catalog update

Triage notes (initial):
- Correlated spike in request queue length for embedding workers in us-west-2 starting ~03:25 UTC. CPU/GPU utilization marginally higher but not saturated.
- Observed a 45% increase in KV-cache miss rate after v20271102-4 rollout (likely changes to tokenization or cache keys).
- Per-batch prep time increased ~3x on the new quantized kernel path (see link to recent job traces in Grafana).

Immediate mitigation options:
1) Canary rollback of model catalog for Logitica traffic to v20271101-9 (will stop routing to v20271102-4). Command: 
   redwood ctl route update --customer logitica --model embeddings --variant v20271101-9 --weight 100
2) Reduce runtime max_batch_size to lower tail latency while we investigate (temp config change, cheaper but may affect throughput).

I'm going to attach a short playbook (rollback-playbook.md) with steps. Planning to attempt an internal canary rollback in 25-30 minutes pending approval.

Marcus
Director, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: mina.haddad@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: 2027-11-03T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency spike — embeddings p95/p99 after yesterday's catalog update

FW: forwarding initial traces from Elena for context.

Quick findings from runtime traces:
- The new kernel selection for v20271102-4 changes the execution path for attention kernels and shifts some work into CPU pre-processing (quantized tensor packing). That increases per-request prep cost, which amplifies tail latency under concurrent loads.
- Our adaptive batching heuristic assumed faster prep and is now creating larger batches than optimal; larger batches + longer prep = long tails.

Immediate actions executed now:
- Decreased adaptive_batch_size upper bound from 128 -> 48 for the affected pool in us-west-2 (will reduce p99 but may reduce throughput).
- Marked Logitica routing to candidate variant as pending rollback (Marcus to execute the route command).

I'll continue with trace-level correlates (spans attached) and a short RCA note.

Neha
SRE
Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@logitica.com>
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.com, sean.gallagher@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2027-11-03T10:30:00-08:00
Subject: Action plan and ETA — Logitica embeddings latency spike

Elena — quick update and mitigation plan: 

1) We will perform a canary rollback of Logitica traffic to the previous catalog artifact (v20271101-9) starting at 10:45 PST (in ~15 minutes). Marcus will run the route update and monitor p95/p99 for 20 minutes.
2) SRE has already reduced adaptive batch size in us-west-2 to reduce tail latency. We expect measurable p95/p99 improvement within the first 10 minutes post-change.
3) If rollback shows improvement, we'll keep Logitica on v20271101-9 while infra/product completes a detailed RCA and kernel analysis.
4) We'll provide a postmortem and root cause within 48 hours.
5) For immediate remediation we can offer a one-time service credit; Jonas will coordinate with your procurement team.

We're also proposing an exec sync between your VP-Eng and our VP-CS / VP-Eng if you'd like — please let us know availability.

Apologies for the disruption. I'll follow up after the canary and share metrics.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Sr. Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: rollback-playbook.md

From: Elena Ruiz <elena@logitica.com>
To: mina.haddad@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@logitica.com
Date: 2027-11-03T12:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Action plan and ETA — Logitica embeddings latency spike

Thanks Mina — appreciate the quick response. Canary rollback is fine. Please escalate to your execs; I have our CTO in the loop for the quarterly review next week and want to ensure this won't be a recurring issue. Jonas, please loop procurement for credit coordination.

We'll standby for the postmortem.

Elena
Head of Engineering — Logitica
